A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDPO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SOTOPIA experiments, Llama and Mistral comparisons, ablations, and manual evaluation of error localization and segment selection.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports a revised dialogue-length control in Figure 3.

M1.justification: Behavioral cloning, error localization, five-session sampling, and equal-length segment selection are unchanged. The SDPO loss in v1 Equation 7 matches v2 Equation 8; expanded theoretical exposition does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions train on SOTOPIA-π and evaluate on SOTOPIA, including its Hard subset, using the same social tasks and interlocutor coverage. The revised dialogue cutoff changes a testing procedure within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same proprietary models, behavioral-cloning models, DPO, ETO, DMPO, and Preferred-SFT comparators. Adding the ETO label to Table 3's existing [m, n] row does not introduce another evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.5 changes the output-length control from terminating after 8 agent turns to 10, explicitly targeting comparable token counts. Dataset splits, evaluation metrics, and the principal training and testing settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The output-length analysis replaces the 8-turn illustration against Llama with a 10-turn control supporting comparison against other multi-turn methods. Other ablations and supplementary analyses remain; the probability-trajectory analysis moves from Section 4.5 to Appendix E.2.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report a single test in Section 4.2 and retain the three-author averages in Appendix C.2. Neither adds repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 3 replaces the 8-turn SDPO result, labeled 7.6 average turns and 51.8 words per turn, with a 10-turn result labeled 9.7 and 50.1, with a different plotted goal score. These are different conditions, not a same-setting improvement. Tables 1–9 and the other result plots retain their numerical findings.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds the explicit length-normalized Bradley–Terry expression in Equation 11, and B.1 states the equal-length condition for ETO–SDPO equivalence. The SAOM framework, discount-factor criticism, and final SDPO loss already appear in v1; much of the remaining mathematical revision is relocation or equivalent restatement.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies training-noise elimination as 'largely' achieved and removes the unconditional statement that full-session SDPO becomes ETO; Appendix B.1 supplies an equal-length qualification. The central segment-level alignment and SOTOPIA superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 now attributes efficient positive-sample use to finer granularity and the theoretically robust loss, replacing that passage's emphasis on constraining interlocutor behavior. The output-efficiency interpretation also shifts toward comparison with other multi-turn methods at similar lengths. Section 7's limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, model-version identifiers, construction prompts, dataset statistics, and the code/data link are retained. Moving the pipeline diagram into the main text does not disclose a new implementation procedure.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bradley–Terry, SimPO, and SePO references, including a brief discussion of selective token optimization, and removes the Jiang et al. Mistral reference. The broader positioning around alignment granularity remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around separate data-granularity and theoretical arguments. DPO background moves into Section 2.3, DMPO material is reorganized across Section 3.3 and Appendix B, and the probability analysis moves to Appendix E.2, substantially changing the explanatory structure.

P2.justification: v2 introduces a new schematic Figure 1, moves the previous overview to appendix Figure 6, promotes the pipeline from appendix Figure 6 to main-text Figure 2, and relocates the training plot to Figure 9. Table 3 is restructured, Table 4 reordered, and Figure 3's annotations revised, substantially reorganizing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The new overview, main-text pipeline, and clearer organization make the method and theoretical comparison easier to follow. Explicit normalization details and the qualified ETO equivalence improve precision, while the revised length control supports a closer comparison with multi-turn baselines. These are limited gains: the underlying method, principal results, evaluation coverage, and single-test reporting remain unchanged.
